_comment: Python claims are the awkward case: staleness here is a RUNTIME property, not a syntax one. The verifier resolves dotted stdlib attributes statically against the installed interpreter (importlib + getattr) and NEVER executes the snippet — see agents/lang/drivers.py PythonDriver. So an 'old' form fails because the attribute does not exist on this interpreter, which is exactly the fact an agent needs.

claims.note: string.maketrans was a Python 2 module function; it is str.maketrans now
asyncio.async() was removed (it was a keyword after 3.5); ensure_future is the survivor
the camelCase deprecated aliases (assertEquals, failUnless) were removed in 3.12
claims.summary: the camelCase aliases (`assertEquals`, `failUnless`) were removed in 3.12 — use `assertEqual`

claims.note: the imp module was removed in 3.12; importlib is the replacement
claims.summary: the `imp` module was removed in 3.12 — use `importlib` (`importlib.import_module`)
